10-01.t: Birth of William Stokes, Pioneer of Thoracic Auscultation
10-01.s: Irish physician William Stokes was born; he promoted percussion and auscultation and co-described Stokes-Adams syndrome (1846) and Cheyne-Stokes respiration (1854).

10-01.t: Madras Medical School Elevated to Madras Medical College
10-01.s: The Madras Medical School was formally accorded college status as Madras Medical College, becoming one of India's earliest premier institutions for modern medical education. Its first batch of diplomates graduated in 1852.

10-01.t: First National Voluntary Blood Donation Day Observed in India
10-01.s: The Indian Society of Blood Transfusion and Immunohaematology initiated the first National Voluntary Blood Donation Day across India to promote safe, non-remunerated blood donation.

10-01.t: Nobel Prize Awarded to James Allison and Tasuku Honjo for Cancer Immunotherapy
10-01.s: The Nobel Assembly awarded the 2018 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine to James P. Allison and Tasuku Honjo for discovering cancer therapy by inhibition of negative immune regulation (checkpoint inhibitors).

10-02.t: Birth of Berkeley Moynihan, Pioneer of Abdominal Surgery
10-02.s: English surgeon Berkeley George Andrew Moynihan was born; he advanced abdominal and hepatobiliary surgery and described Moynihan's sign and Moynihan's hump of the right hepatic artery.

10-02.t: Launch of Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS)
10-02.s: The Government of India launched the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme to combat malnutrition, reduce infant and maternal mortality, and deliver supplementary nutrition and health check-ups through Anganwadi centres.

10-02.t: Death of Dr. Mary Poonen Lukose, India's First Female Surgeon General
10-02.s: Dr. Mary Poonen Lukose, pioneering gynaecologist, founder of the Tuberculosis Sanatorium in Nagercoil, and the first woman appointed Surgeon General in India (Travancore, 1938), passed away at age 90.

10-02.t: Launch of the Pulse Polio Immunisation Programme in Delhi
10-02.s: India rolled out its first Pulse Polio Immunisation drive in Delhi, administering oral polio drops across 4,000 booths and laying the foundation for the nationwide campaign that eventually eradicated wild poliovirus from India.

10-02.t: Nobel Prize Awarded to Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman for mRNA Vaccines
10-02.s: The Nobel Assembly awarded the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine to Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman for discoveries concerning nucleoside base modifications that enabled effective mRNA vaccines against COVID-19.

10-03.t: First Issue of the British Medical Journal Published
10-03.s: The Provincial Medical and Surgical Journal published its first issue (Vol. 1, No. 1), later adopting the title British Medical Journal (BMJ) in 1857.

10-03.t: Death of Dr. Kadambini Ganguly, India's First Practicing Female Physician
10-03.s: Dr. Kadambini Ganguly, one of India's first two female doctors of Western medicine and the first woman admitted to Calcutta Medical College (1883), passed away in Calcutta after performing a surgical operation the same day.

10-03.t: Birth of Kanupriya Agarwal (Durga), India's First IVF Baby
10-03.s: Dr. Subhash Mukhopadhyay and colleagues achieved the birth of Kanupriya Agarwal ('Durga') in Kolkata via in-vitro fertilisation, making her India's first and the world's second test-tube baby.

10-03.t: Nobel Prize Awarded to Svante Pääbo for Paleogenomics
10-03.s: Swedish geneticist Svante Pääbo won the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for sequencing the Neanderthal genome and discovering the Denisovan hominin.

10-04.t: Birth of Alan L. Hart, Pioneer of Tuberculosis Radiology Screening
10-04.s: American physician and radiologist Alan L. Hart was born; he pioneered the use of chest X-ray screening to detect tuberculosis early and curb its spread.

10-04.t: Nobel Prize Awarded to David Julius and Ardem Patapoutian
10-04.s: David Julius and Ardem Patapoutian were awarded the 2021 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering the cellular receptors for temperature and mechanical touch.

10-05.t: The Lancet Publishes Its First Issue
10-05.s: Founded by Thomas Wakley, The Lancet published its inaugural issue (Vol. 1, No. 1), launching a new era of independent medical journalism and healthcare reform.

10-05.t: Nobel Prize Awarded for Discovery of Hepatitis C Virus
10-05.s: Harvey J. Alter, Michael Houghton, and Charles M. Rice were awarded the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for the discovery of the Hepatitis C virus.

10-06.t: Birth of Wilhelm von Waldeyer-Hartz, Coiner of 'Neuron' and 'Chromosome'
10-06.s: German anatomist Wilhelm Gottfried Waldeyer-Hartz was born; he described Waldeyer's tonsillar ring (1884) and popularized the neuron theory.

10-06.t: Nobel Prize Awarded for Peripheral Immune Tolerance
10-06.s: Mary E. Brunkow, Frederick J. Ramsdell, and Shimon Sakaguchi were awarded the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries concerning peripheral immune tolerance and regulatory T cells.

10-07.t: Jules Tinel Publishes Description of Tinel's Sign
10-07.s: French neurologist Jules Tinel published 'Le signe du fourmillement dans les lésions des nerfs périphériques,' describing distal tingling elicited by percussing an injured peripheral nerve.

10-07.t: Nobel Prize Awarded for Cellular Oxygen Sensing
10-07.s: William G. Kaelin Jr., Sir Peter J. Ratcliffe, and Gregg L. Semenza were awarded the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering how cells sense and adapt to oxygen availability.

10-08.t: Birth of George Henry Fox, Co-Describer of Fox-Fordyce Disease
10-08.s: American dermatologist George Henry Fox was born; he was a pioneer of dermatologic photography and co-described Fox-Fordyce disease in 1902.

10-08.t: Birth of Dr. G. N. Ramachandran, Structural Biology Pioneer
10-08.s: Born in Ernakulam, Dr. G. N. Ramachandran revolutionized molecular biophysics by proposing the triple-helical structure of collagen and creating the Ramachandran plot for analyzing peptide conformations.

10-08.t: Death of Sir Henry Head, Pioneer of Sensory Neuroanatomy
10-08.s: English neurologist Sir Henry Head died; he mapped human dermatomes, characterized visceral referred pain (Head's zones), and co-described autonomic dysreflexia (Head-Riddoch syndrome).

10-09.t: Death of Gabriele Falloppio, Discoverer of the Fallopian Tubes
10-09.s: Italian anatomist and physician Gabriele Falloppio died; he provided the first accurate anatomical description of the uterine (Fallopian) tubes and several cranial nerves.

10-09.t: Birth of Ralph Milton Waters, Founder of Academic Anesthesiology
10-09.s: American anesthesiologist Ralph Milton Waters was born; he founded the first academic anesthesiology program at the University of Wisconsin and invented the Waters CO2 absorption canister.

10-10.t: Birth of Octave Landry, First Describer of Guillain-Barré Syndrome
10-10.s: French physician Jean-Baptiste Octave Landry de Thézillat was born; in 1859 he published the first clinical description of acute ascending paralysis, later known as Guillain-Barré syndrome.

10-10.t: Founding of SICOT, International Orthopedic Surgery Society
10-10.s: An international group of orthopedic surgeons met at the Hôtel Crillon in Paris to found SICOT (Société Internationale de Chirurgie Orthopédique et de Traumatologie).

10-11.t: Death of Irving Freiler Stein, Co-Describer of PCOS
10-11.s: American gynecologist Irving Freiler Stein died; alongside Michael Leventhal, he characterized polycystic ovary syndrome (Stein-Leventhal syndrome) in 1934.

10-11.t: Death of John Hilton Edwards, Describer of Trisomy 18
10-11.s: English geneticist John Hilton Edwards died; in 1960 he first described Trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), a major chromosomal disorder.

10-12.t: Birth of René Leriche, Pioneer of Vascular Surgery
10-12.s: French surgeon Henri Marie René Leriche was born; he described aortoiliac occlusive disease (Leriche syndrome) in 1940 and advanced sympathectomy and vascular surgery.

10-12.t: First Clinical Use of the Iron Lung Respirator
10-12.s: The Drinker-Shaw negative-pressure iron lung respirator was used for the first time at Boston Children's Hospital to support a young girl with respiratory paralysis from polio.

10-13.t: Birth of Rudolf Virchow, Founder of Cellular Pathology
10-13.s: German physician and pathologist Rudolf Virchow was born in Schivelbein; he revolutionized pathology by demonstrating that diseases arise from abnormalities within individual cells.

10-13.t: CDC Obtains First Electron Micrograph of Ebola Virus
10-13.s: Researchers at the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) obtained the first electron micrograph of an Ebola viral particle during the initial 1976 outbreak.

10-14.t: Birth of Armand Trousseau, Master Clinician
10-14.s: French physician Armand Trousseau was born; he described Trousseau's sign of latent tetany (1861) and Trousseau's syndrome of migratory thrombophlebitis associated with occult malignancy.

10-14.t: Birth of C. Everett Koop, 13th U.S. Surgeon General
10-14.s: American pediatric surgeon and public health leader Charles Everett Koop was born; as U.S. Surgeon General (1982-1989), he led major public health campaigns on HIV/AIDS and tobacco.

10-15.t: Birth of Augusta Déjerine-Klumpke, Neuroanatomy Pioneer
10-15.s: American-born French neurologist Augusta Déjerine-Klumpke was born; she described lower brachial plexus palsy (Klumpke's palsy) in 1885 and co-authored landmark neuroanatomy texts.

The Global Public-Private Partnership for Handwashing launched the inaugural Global Handwashing Day to promote handwashing with soap as an effective, low-cost intervention against infectious diseases.

10-16.t: First Public Demonstration of Surgical Ether Anesthesia ('Ether Day')
10-16.s: Dentist William T. G. Morton administered diethyl ether to a patient while surgeon John Collins Warren excised a neck tumor at Massachusetts General Hospital, inaugurating modern surgical anesthesia.

10-16.t: Death of Dr. Dilip Mahalanabis, Pioneer of Oral Rehydration Therapy
10-16.s: Indian paediatrician Dr. Dilip Mahalanabis, whose field deployment of Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) during the 1971 refugee crisis saved millions of lives worldwide from cholera and diarrheal dehydration, died in Kolkata.

10-17.t: Birth of Sir Robert Reynolds Macintosh, Inventor of the Curved Laryngoscope
10-17.s: New Zealand-born anesthetist Sir Robert Reynolds Macintosh was born; he invented the curved Macintosh laryngoscope blade in 1943 and helped establish Oxford's chair of anesthetics.

10-17.t: Death of Santiago Ramón y Cajal, Father of Modern Neuroscience
10-17.s: Spanish neuroscientist and pathologist Santiago Ramón y Cajal died; he established the neuron doctrine and won the 1906 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

10-17.t: Dedication of the All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA) in New Delhi
10-17.s: On the second National Ayurveda Day, the All India Institute of Ayurveda in New Delhi was dedicated to the nation as an apex autonomous institute for postgraduate education, research, and integrative clinical care.

10-18.t: Death of Philipp Franz von Siebold, Introducer of Western Medicine to Japan
10-18.s: German physician and botanist Philipp Franz von Siebold died; he taught Western clinical medicine and surgery in Nagasaki, influencing modern Japanese medical practice.

10-18.t: Founding of the Calcutta School of Medicine (Now R. G. Kar Medical College)
10-18.s: Dr. Radha Gobinda Kar and fellow Indian physicians founded the Calcutta School of Medicine, establishing Asia's first private medical college to advance self-sufficiency in medical education.

10-18.t: Death of Alfred Binet, Creator of the First Practical Intelligence Test
10-18.s: French psychologist Alfred Binet died; alongside Théodore Simon, he developed the Binet-Simon scale, the foundation of modern standardized cognitive and intelligence testing.

10-19.t: Streptomycin Isolated by Rutgers University Researchers
10-19.s: Researchers at Rutgers University isolated streptomycin, the first aminoglycoside antibiotic and the first effective antimicrobial treatment for tuberculosis.

10-19.t: Death of Philip Drinker, Co-Inventor of the Iron Lung
10-19.s: American industrial hygienist and chemical engineer Philip Drinker died; he co-invented the Drinker respirator (iron lung) in 1928 to sustain patients with polio-induced respiratory paralysis.

10-20.t: Birth of Thomas Bartholin, Discoverer of the Human Lymphatic System
10-20.s: Danish physician and anatomist Thomas Bartholin was born; he published the first full description of the human lymphatic system and documented refrigeration anesthesia in 1661.

10-20.t: Birth of Austin Flint, Describer of the Austin Flint Murmur
10-20.s: American physician Austin Flint was born; he promoted the binaural stethoscope and described the Austin Flint diastolic murmur associated with severe aortic regurgitation in 1862.

10-21.t: Birth of Caleb Hillier Parry, Early Describer of Graves' Disease
10-21.s: English physician Caleb Hillier Parry was born; his posthumous 1825 papers contained early clinical descriptions of hyperthyroid goiter (Parry's disease) and Hirschsprung's disease.

10-21.t: Birth of Oswald Avery, Pioneer Who Proved DNA Carries Genetic Information
10-21.s: Canadian-born American physician and researcher Oswald Theodore Avery was born; his 1944 experiments demonstrated that DNA, rather than protein, is the transforming principle of heredity.

10-21.t: India Surpasses 1 Billion (100 Crore) COVID-19 Vaccine Doses
10-21.s: India's nationwide COVID-19 immunization campaign crossed the landmark milestone of 100 crore (one billion) cumulative vaccine doses administered.

10-22.t: Ralph Huber Patented the Non-Coring Hypodermic Needle Point
10-22.s: Ralph Lee Huber received a U.S. patent for a curved, non-coring hypodermic needle tip ('Huber point') that prevented tissue plugging and later formed the basis of the Tuohy epidural needle.

10-22.t: Death of Albert Szent-Györgyi, Discoverer of Vitamin C
10-22.s: Hungarian biochemist Albert Szent-Györgyi died; he won the 1937 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for isolating vitamin C (ascorbic acid) and elucidating biological oxidation.

10-23.t: Birth of Moritz Kaposi, Describer of Kaposi Sarcoma
10-23.s: Hungarian dermatologist Moritz Kaposi was born; he first described idiopathic multiple pigmented sarcoma of the skin, now known as Kaposi sarcoma, in 1872.

10-23.t: Birth of Charles Clifford Macklin, Describer of the Macklin Effect
10-23.s: Canadian pulmonologist Charles Clifford Macklin was born; in 1939 he explained the mechanism of alveolar rupture and air dissection leading to pneumomediastinum (the Macklin effect).

10-24.t: Birth of Antonie van Leeuwenhoek, Father of Microbiology
10-24.s: Dutch microscopist Antonie van Leeuwenhoek was born; using handcrafted single-lens microscopes, he became the first person to observe and document bacteria, protozoa, and muscle fibers.

10-24.t: World Polio Day Observed Globally in Honor of Jonas Salk
10-24.s: Observed annually on October 24 to commemorate Jonas Salk's birthday month and mobilize global efforts by Rotary International, WHO, and UNICEF toward complete polio eradication.

10-25.t: Death of Harold Leeming Sheehan, Describer of Sheehan Syndrome
10-25.s: English pathologist Harold Leeming Sheehan died; in 1937 he described postpartum pituitary necrosis (Sheehan syndrome) following severe obstetric hemorrhage.

10-25.t: Dame Averil Mansfield Appointed First Female Professor of Surgery in the UK
10-25.s: Vascular surgeon Dame Averil Mansfield became the first woman appointed Professor of Surgery in the United Kingdom, marking a milestone for women in academic surgical leadership.

10-26.t: Death of Waldemar Haffkine, Developer of India's Plague Vaccine
10-26.s: Bacteriologist Waldemar Haffkine, who conducted cholera vaccine trials in India in 1893 and developed the bubonic plague vaccine at Grant Medical College, Bombay in 1897 (founding what became the Haffkine Institute), died in Lausanne.

10-26.t: Last Natural Case of Smallpox (Ali Maow Maalin)
10-26.s: Hospital cook Ali Maow Maalin developed a smallpox rash in Merka, Somalia, marking the world's last naturally acquired case of variola minor and a decisive milestone toward global eradication.

10-26.t: Leonard Bailey Performs Baboon-to-Human Heart Transplant on 'Baby Fae'
10-26.s: At Loma Linda University Medical Center, surgeon Leonard L. Bailey transplanted a baboon heart into a 12-day-old infant with hypoplastic left heart syndrome ('Baby Fae'), a landmark xenotransplantation case.

10-27.t: Death of Michael Servetus, First European to Describe Pulmonary Circulation
10-27.s: Spanish physician and theologian Michael Servetus was executed in Geneva; in his writings he became the first European to accurately describe pulmonary circulation of blood from the heart through the lungs.

10-27.t: Donora Smog Disaster Begins in Pennsylvania
10-27.s: A severe industrial temperature-inversion smog trapped toxic pollutants over Donora, Pennsylvania, killing 20 people and sickening thousands, catalyzing modern U.S. air pollution and environmental health legislation.

10-28.t: Birth of Henry Koplik, Describer of Koplik Spots in Measles
10-28.s: American pediatrician Henry Koplik was born; in 1896 he described the pathognomonic oral mucosal lesions (Koplik spots) that appear prior to the measles skin rash.

10-28.t: Birth of Jonas Salk, Developer of the Inactivated Polio Vaccine
10-28.s: American virologist Jonas Salk was born in New York City; he developed the first safe and effective inactivated polio vaccine (1955), transforming global pediatric public health.

10-28.t: First National Ayurveda Day Observed in India
10-28.s: The Ministry of AYUSH inaugurated India's first National Ayurveda Day, launching 'Mission Madhumeha through Ayurveda' and releasing national protocols for diabetes prevention and control.

10-29.t: Death of Wilhelm Heinrich Erb, Pioneer of Electrodiagnosis
10-29.s: German neurologist Wilhelm Heinrich Erb died; he pioneered clinical electrotherapy and described Erb-Duchenne brachial plexus palsy and limb-girdle muscular dystrophy.

10-29.t: Death of Joseph Babinski, Describer of the Babinski Reflex
10-29.s: French neurologist Joseph Jules François Félix Babinski died; he discovered the plantar extensor response (Babinski sign) indicating corticospinal tract dysfunction.

10-30.t: Birth of Dickinson W. Richards Jr., Cardiac Catheterization Laureate
10-30.s: American physician Dickinson Woodruff Richards Jr. was born; he shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with André Cournand and Werner Forssmann for developing cardiac catheterization.

10-30.t: U.S. National Doctors' Day Signed into Federal Law
10-30.s: President George H. W. Bush signed legislation designating March 30 as U.S. National Doctors' Day to honor physicians and commemorate the first surgical use of ether anesthesia in 1842.

10-31.t: Birth of Paolo Mantegazza, Early Researcher of Cocaine's Physiological Effects
10-31.s: Italian neurologist and physiologist Paolo Mantegazza was born; in 1859 he published early experimental observations on the physiological and neuropsychiatric effects of coca leaves.

10-31.t: Birth of Adolf von Baeyer, Organic Chemist and Barbituric Acid Pioneer
10-31.s: German chemist Adolf von Baeyer was born; his synthesis of barbituric acid and organic ring structures laid the groundwork for barbiturate sedatives and modern medicinal chemistry.

10-31.t: Birth of Dr. Khwaja Abdul Hamied, Founder of Cipla
10-31.s: Born in Aligarh, industrial and pharmaceutical chemist Dr. Khwaja Abdul Hamied founded Cipla in 1935, laying a cornerstone for indigenous pharmaceutical manufacturing and affordable generic medicines in India.
